transcript:
Header: 2026-04-29 15:00 PDT | Duration 65m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Lena Martinez (Redwood AE); Samir Patel (Redwood SE); Aisha Khan (Zenith AI, Dir of AI); Mark Rivers (Zenith, SRE); Tobias Lee (Zenith, Product)

Summary: Kickoff for a 6-week POC focused on inference performance and cost tradeoffs for a user-facing search/chat feature. Confirmed timeline, access steps, dataset and benchmark definitions, midpoint review cadence, and exec readout requirements. Some audio dropouts around 00:18 and occasional mis-transcripts.

Topics: POC scope, success criteria, workload sizing, baseline benchmarks, access/credentials, security checks, milestone dates, exec readout expectations

[00:00] Lena Martinez: All right everyone, thanks for joining. This is Lena from Redwood, im the AE on the account, that is Samir our solutions engineer, he'll run through the technical plan. Um quick intros?
[00:18] Aisha Khan: Hi all, Aisha here, director of AI. We're looking to validate inferencing economics for our next-release chat and search feature, mostly latency and hallucination rate.
[00:27] Mark Rivers: Mark, SRE, i'll own network and access.
[00:31] Tobias Lee: Tobias, product. We'll present to VP of Product at exec readout.
[00:35] Samir Patel: Hey, Samir. Quick agenda: kickoff goals, baseline runs, what success looks like, access checklist, milestone calendar, open questions.

[00:47] Lena: High level p-o-c is 6 weeks, but we want clear gates. Week zero kickoff, week one access + baseline, week two baseline benchmarking, week three mid-point review and optimize, week four tuning and reruns, week five final benchmark, week six exec readout and acceptance. Does that line up with expectations?
[01:07] Aisha: Yeah, that timeline looks good. We need a fast win within two weeks so execs dont freak out.
[01:12] Tobias: Also want a simple go/no-go metric for the exec — like p95 latency under 200ms for interactive flows and no more than 3% hallucination on our test set.
[01:20] Samir: That's doable. For clarity, when you say hallucination rate, is that manually labeled false responses or policy-based false acceptance?
[01:27] Aisha: We'll use manual labels from our QA team on a 5k sample and a secondary automated rubric for scale.

[01:33] Mark: On the infra side, we'll provision a peered VPC and a service account. Do you need dedicated capacity or can we start on hosted?
[01:41] Samir: Start on hosted API to get baseline numbers, we can transition to Redwood Dedicated if the throughput/latency tradeoffs need it. Note though hosted runs cost more per-token for high sustained throughput.
[01:52] Lena: We'll recommend a two-track run: hosted for speed of iteration and a single Dedicated sizing run to estimate committed costs.

[02:01] Tobias: Workload sizing - our production expectation is about 50 rps peak for the chat front-end, average payload ~600 tokens, but there's a bursty pattern with peaks up to 90 rps.
[02:14] Samir: Good to know. For benchmarking we'll run 1) single-request latency distributions, 2) sustained throughput at 50 and 90 rps, 3) 10k prompt quality sweep, and 4) KV cache warm vs cold scenarios. We'll share a perf-run template.
[02:31] Aisha: Also log-level tracing and token-level cost breakdown are must-haves for the readout.

[02:38] Lena: Success criteria proposal: p95 latency < 200ms for conversational rerank flows, 99th under 350ms for the heavy request, quality pass rate >= 97% on labeled rubric, cost per 1k tokens below threshold X (we'll fill X after initial baseline). If any of these fail we escalate to a remediation sprint.
[02:56] Tobias: Agree but can we add an availability SLA gate, like less than 1% errors during sustained load?
[03:03] Samir: Yep, availability SLO included. We'll also capture error taxonomy.

[03:10] Mark: Security checklist — SSO/SAML for console access, audit logs, KMS for keys, optional VPC peering. We may need to see SOC 2 and ISO docs.
[03:20] Lena: We'll send the security pack and SOC 2 attestation. Also note that private deployment option exists if compliance requires on-prem.
[03:28] Aisha: Can you include details on data handling — retention, logs, whether embeddings are persisted?
[03:33] Samir: Short answer: by default hosted keeps minimal logs for X days, embeddings can be configured to not be stored. We'll document the retention options and KMS flows.

[03:42] Lena: Access items: 1) service account IAM and S3 write access for Redwood to pull test data, 2) VPC peering details if you want private egress, 3) SAML SSO test account for the console, 4) sample dataset upload to the provided S3 path. Mark, you will own the infra checklist, right?
[03:58] Mark: Yep, will share ticket by Monday. Expect some firewall rules, allowlist IPs, and a short window for peering.

[04:06] Samir: For the actual benchmark, we prefer reproducible load using our runner. We'll give a dockerized harness and a JMX-style script. Runs will capture token-level latency, model variant, quantization flags, and KV cache state. A note — sometimes transcripts call it K-V cash, so dont fret if that shows up in notes.
[04:26] Tobias: Good to know. How do we score hallucination? Manual labeling then aggregate F1 or pass/fail?
[04:33] Samir: We'll use the labeled pass rate plus a severity-weighted score. For readout, a single pass rate metric is easier for execs, with a breakdown in the appendix.

[04:43] Aisha: Who's presenting the midpoint? I want a stripe-like short readout for execs.
[04:48] Lena: Midpoint we'll do a 30-minute technical review with SE+customer SMEs, then a short 15-min exec sync if numbers look promising. Full exec readout at the end of week six.

[04:59] Tobias: For the exec readout, we need clear ask: decision to go to Dedicated commit, or continue hosted with caching, plus recommended cost commitment.
[05:08] Lena: We'll prepare a one-pager with recommended commit scenarios and model tradeoffs.

[05:13] Mark: Any compliance gating we should know now that would block access? Some of our customers require lateral isolation and an audit trail.
[05:21] Samir: We can enable audit logging and KMS-backed keys. If they need full air-gapped, see Private deployment but that adds lead time.

[05:29] Aisha: Timeline specifics and dates?
[05:31] Lena: Proposed dates: kickoff today 2026-04-29, access completed by 2026-05-04, baseline runs 2026-05-05 through 2026-05-12, mid-point review 2026-05-20, optimization window 2026-05-21 to 2026-05-28, final benchmark 2026-05-29 to 2026-05-31, exec readout week of 2026-06-02. All flexible but we want firm windows for exec scheduling.
[06:04] Tobias: Midpoint on 05-20 works. I will invite our VP of Product to the final readout.
[06:10] Lena: Great. A couple of open questions — dataset size for initial runs, what model families you want us to include, and how strict the quality gate is.
[06:19] Aisha: Start with 5k labeled prompts, expand to 10k for final. Use the Llama-3 family and a smaller quantized variant for cost comparison. Also include one Anthropic or OpenAI baseline if we can get permission to run them in the same harness for apples-to-apples.
[06:36] Samir: We'll include open baselines where permitted. Note that API keys and TOS may limit what we can run. We'll document that in the runbook.

[06:44] Mark: Any risk dependencies? I see two main ones: delays in VPC peering and dataset delivery.
[06:50] Lena: Agreed. We'll target fast tracks: hosted runs don't need peering so we can start quality runs immediately. Dedicated capacity sizing requires more lead time.

[06:58] Tobias: On remediation, if the quality metric misses the threshold at mid-point, what's the cadence to iterate?
[07:03] Samir: We'll run a two-week remediation sprint: tuning prompts, quantization profiles, caching strategy, and a re-benchmark. If still failing, escalate to architecture review and consider a Dedicated lane.

[07:14] Aisha: Ok, good. Recording that.

[07:17] Lena: Quick recap of next steps: Redwood to send benchmark template and runbook by 2026-05-06, Zenith to upload 5k sample and open infra ticket by 2026-05-04, schedule mid-point review 2026-05-20 and tentatively book exec readout week of 2026-06-02.
[07:33] Samir: I'll attach the perf harness repo, a run script, and a sample results spreadsheet. Also include a checklist for Dedicated sizing.

[07:41] Tobias: Can we get an estimate of cost delta between hosted and a 2x Dedicated reservation for our workload?
[07:47] Lena: We'll include a cost scenarios page in the one-pager. It will show unit cost per 1k tokens, projected monthly spend at 50 rps, and breakeven points for reserved capacity.

[07:57] Aisha: One last ask — include a simple storyboard for execs showing user impact, latency improvements, and cost tradeoffs.
[08:03] Lena: Will do. Any other questions?
[08:06] Mark: No, that's it.
[08:08] Lena: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the materials. Meeting adjourned.

Action summary (in transcript): Samir to provide runner and spreadsheet; Lena to send SOW/acceptance criteria and security pack; Zenith to provision infra and upload dataset. Midpoint review 2026-05-20. Exec readout week of 2026-06-02.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional word swaps (quantization heard as quan-tize-ation), speaker tag drift at 00:18, two short audio dropouts.
